title: Austin Market Relocation & City Services Debate
summary:
• **Market Location Controversy**: Multiple petitions regarding the city market's location were debated—vegetable dealers opposed moving it while citizens protested establishing it at the "Alliance Yard" block. All petitions were referred to committee for further review.

• **Infrastructure & Wagon Scales**: The council approved two wagon scale installations (at Lavaca & 8th and Chicon & 6th Streets) to help regulate commerce in the growing city, with government supervision required.

• **Police Force Election & Controversy**: The council held elections to fill police positions, with debate over Sergeant Owens' reinstatement after suspension. Council members voted to pay him his back salary and confirmed 10 officers for the next term.

• **Congress Avenue Storm Sewer Decision**: Following heated debate with multiple failed motions, the council adopted original plans and specifications for a storm sewer contract with contractor Wm. Field and authorized a committee to finalize the agreement.

• **Park Improvements**: The council approved funding for Peace Park improvements ($600) and authorized hiring a manager, while thanking citizen volunteers for their work on the park.

The Chair laid before the Council the following communication which was read and ordered

Austin, Texas, May 5th 1903
Do the Hon City Council of the City of Austin; Austin, Texas,
Gentlemen!
In relinquishing the office of City Treasurer, Daffy Communication I do most regretfully,
I cannot refrain from ex-Treasurer from an expression of the gratitude which I feel
towards the members of the City Council, who have ever lent their best efforts towards the
maintenance of the peace and harmony which has done so much in assisting and encouraging
me during my incumbency.
In my short time which I have had the good fortune to be associated with you, my relations
have been most pleasant and I believe the advice has been satisfactory.
To the Finance Committee, Composed of Messrs Madden, Schneider, Moore, and to the City
Clerk, Mr Johnson, I desire especially to express my grateful thanks for the assistance
rendered me, without which
I should have been sorely tried.
With the Kindest regards to each and all of you, with renewed expressions of appreciation
and assuring you that at any time I can be of service to you, it shall be my pleasure to
act
I beg to remain
Very Sincerely
W.H. Fults
